decisions.reason: As an incremental extension of the core heat-exchange portfolio in a growing market, it shows no clear performance shortfall versus aspiration and the firm's current expansion and technical slack justify continued commercialization.

This condenser is close to the firm's established competencies, and with no evidence yet of results below aspiration, a boundedly rational management would keep it while learning from the market under favorable industry conditions.
Because it is adjacent to the existing offer and the firm has R&D capacity, service support, and organizational slack, management would continue it unless clearer signs of underperformance emerge.

The tube-liner product builds directly on the firm's installed-base service business, so its strategic fit is strong and there is no indication that it falls short enough of aspirations to trigger withdrawal.

A customized industrial air cooler matches the firm's solution-oriented business model, and in the absence of negative performance evidence management would retain it to exploit customer-specific demand and learning effects.
Repair inserts fit the firm's lifecycle-services and retrofit strengths especially well, and with industry growth and available slack there is little reason to redeploy these resources away so early.
